And also in the cities of the Franks:

And in Laodicea, only the great church remained,
and all those who were inside it were saved.
And the earth was split open in it,
and an abyss was seen full of mud,
and in the midst of the mud, a cast statue standing upright.
And likewise most of Antioch and of Tripoli was ruined.
And in this year Joscelin died while a prisoner in Aleppo,
after a complete repentance,
as Ignatius, bishop of Aleppo, said,
who gave him the Mysteries.
And in this year Sultan Muḥammad, son of Sultan Maḥmūd, came with a large army against Baghdad,
and he encamped against it for four months,
and pressed it hard in battle.
Then the Caliph, when he had persuaded the Sultan's nobles with gifts,
held him back from battle.
And news also came to them
that his brother Malikshāh had seized Hamadān and plundered it,
and had also captured the wives of the nobles.
Then the Sultan grew slack,
and departed from Baghdad.
And the forces of the Baghdadis pursued after him,
and whomsoever of the Turks they captured,
they killed without mercy,
because those Turks had done great destruction on the western side of Baghdad where they were encamped;
for inside the mosques they committed fornication with men's wives in full view of their husbands, besides the many murders and burning of houses that they committed.
And in this year died Sultan Sanjar, son of Malikshāh, son of Alp Arslān, son of David,
after he had been delivered from the hands of the Ghuzz, who had imprisoned him.
And in the year 1470
of the Greeks,
Manuel, king of the Greeks, went out to Cilicia,
and Thoros the Armenian fled.
And that king took control over Tarsus and Anazarba and the rest of the cities,
and he remained there the whole winter.
And there came to him the king of Jerusalem and [the prince] of Antioch with the patriarch of the Franks,
and they made peace with him,
and reconciled him with Thoros,
and brought him to him,
and he made him commander of all the cities of the Greeks on the seacoast.
